claim_reviews.conclusion: “Exam paper” correctly matches the specified sense: a paper containing questions for an examination.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Lembar soal” is a natural Indonesian expression for an examination question sheet. “Naskah soal” is also frequent in formal assessment contexts, but its existence does not invalidate “lembar soal.”
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer: lembar soal

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Kertas soalan” is an established Malaysian Malay term for an examination question paper.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian answer: kertas soalan

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Different-common-word” is acceptable for the contrasting head nouns lembar versus kertas, although both expressions share the cognate soal/soalan element. There is no material false-friend contrast.
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation and false-friend contrast

response.rationale: Both answers fit the specified sense of an examination question paper. Indonesian “lembar soal” is attested for an exam question sheet, while Malaysian “kertas soalan” is an established official term. “Naskah soal” is also common in Indonesian institutional contexts, but this is a noncritical alternative, not an error. The different-common-word relation is defensible, and no false-friend contrast is present.
